page: Microsoft Azure D160ads_v7 is an enterprise-scale, general-purpose virtual machine deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. It provisions 160 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 80 physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. The CPU feature set incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512-VNNI, and AVX512-BF16 for vector and integer math acceleration, complemented by dedicated cryptographic extensions such as AES and SHA-NI.

System memory totals 640 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The platform delivers uncached read memory bandwidth of 464.15 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 210.38 GB/sec. Unlike diskless VM configurations, the D160ads_v7 integrates 9,448 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, providing substantial low-latency scratch space directly adjacent to the compute cores. The instance contains zero GPUs and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position the D160ads_v7 in the top decile across virtually all compute, memory, and concurrency metrics. In stress-ng testing, it achieves 3,783.98 points in single-core and 287,722.37 points in multi-core throughput. Geekbench scores reach 2,881 single-core and 28,933 multi-core, with high compilation throughput reaching 88,442 in Clang. In memory-bound transaction benchmarks, the platform processed 204.26 million Redis SET operations per second and handled 41,388.04 database operations in PassMark. CPU-driven inference benchmarks demonstrate 370.19 tokens per second for prompt processing on 7B parameter models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high density by consolidating large core counts, memory, and nearly 9.5 TB of direct NVMe storage onto a single virtual node. This consolidation reduces overhead associated with distributed cluster orchestration. The primary technical tradeoff is the absence of discrete GPU acceleration, constraining massive machine learning training to CPU execution. It is suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching layers, massive CI/CD compilation pipelines, high-throughput web serving, and ETL data processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D160ads_v7 is a high-density, general-purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz. It provides 160 dedicated vCPUs across 80 physical cores, 640 GB of RAM, and 9,448 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX-512, AVX512-VNNI, and hardware encryption extensions. Benchmark results demonstrate top-decile performance across single-core and multi-core evaluations, including 28,933 in Geekbench multi-core and 204.26 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside uncached memory read bandwidth of 464.15 GB/sec. While lacking GPU acceleration, its consolidation of massive compute, balanced memory density, and substantial local scratch disk space delivers solid qualitative cost efficiency for large monolithic workloads. The instance is recommended for enterprise database deployments, in-memory key-value data stores, distributed compilation pipelines, and demanding web scale data infrastructure.
